narratives.Description: bug(verify): verify:orphan-active silently skips briefs whose forge origin it cannot resolve
narratives.Overview:
# `verify:orphan-active` treats "I cannot resolve this brief" as "nothing to report"

A brief whose forge origin the evaluator cannot resolve is counted and skipped. It is never assessed and never becomes a finding. The gate then exits 0 while printing, in its own output, that it did not look at one of the briefs it scanned.

That is the wrong default. A brief Directive cannot resolve is exactly the brief most likely to be malformed, and it is the one case the sweep passes over.

## Measured

Installed npm artifact, `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.1` (dist, not a source checkout — line numbers below are dist).

`orphan-active/evaluate.js:421`:

```js
scanned += 1;
if (issues.length === 0 && prs.length === 0) {
    noOrigin += 1;
    continue;          // never assessed, never reported
}
const assessment = assessOrphanSignature(issues, prs, ctx, issueFilter, tally);
```

`noOrigin` reaches the operator only through an informational basis line (`evaluate.js:211`). It does not affect findings and does not affect the exit code.

## Live reproduction

A consumer repo had one active/running brief for work that had already merged. The gate passed:

```
verify:orphan-active: no orphaned active/running xBRIEFs (scanned 2 running briefs in active/).
  Basis: inventory 1.
  Origins: 1 of 2 scanned briefs resolved zero forge origins.
```

The brief sat in `active/` consuming WIP for the better part of a day, describing work that was already in `master`. The gate reported the blind spot in the same breath as the all-clear.

## Counterfactual

The brief carried a PR reference typed `x-xbrief/pull-request` instead of the canonical `x-xbrief/github-pr`, so `collectGithubRefs` returned `{issues: [], prs: []}`. Changing only that string, in a checksummed copy, and re-running the same gate:

```
verify:orphan-active: 1 active/running xBRIEF look shipped but still consume WIP
  Offending briefs:
    - xbrief/active/<brief>.xbrief.json (linked PR #5 is merged)
```

Restored byte-exact afterwards (sha256 verified). One wrong word in a type string is the whole difference between caught and invisible. The detection logic was correct and ready; it was never reached.

## Why the neighbouring gates do not cover it

- **#3875** — `verify:pr-closeout-attestable` exists and is unwired. Even wired, it triggers on the PR's closing reference. The PR here had `closingIssuesReferences: []` (a dependency-upgrade PR, no `Closes #N`). Brief-bearing work with no closing issue is outside that trigger by construction.
- **#3791** — automating the post-merge sweep routes through this same evaluator, so an originless brief stays skipped however the sweep is invoked.
- **#3495** — the mirror case (work with no brief). This is a brief with no resolvable origin.
- **#3790** — misattribution of resolved orphans, a different failure.

## Suggested shape

Do not silently continue. An originless active/running brief should surface as its own finding kind, distinct from a confirmed orphan, because the remedy is different: the brief needs a usable origin reference (or a deliberate "no forge origin" marker), not `scope:complete`.

Whether it should fail closed or warn is a judgement for maintainers. What should not survive is the current state, where the count is computed, printed, and then dropped on the floor.

Related: #3875, #3791, #3495, #3790, #3913.

## Gate stamp

P1 is the measured consumer miss: one active/running brief for already-merged work, gate printed `no orphaned active/running xBRIEFs` plus `Origins: 1 of 2 scanned briefs resolved zero forge origins`, exit 0. The brief used `x-xbrief/pull-request` instead of `x-xbrief/github-pr`. Changing only that type string made the same gate fail closed on linked PR merged. Companion write-side is #4698; this arc is the skip, not the schema.

Pin-read at dispatch-sha edf1d698aafcf956cff08ad3ad14ff608505861a:

- packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts: after collectGithubRefs, `if (issues.length === 0 && prs.length === 0) { noOrigin += 1; continue; }` never calls assessOrphanSignature. noOrigin is basis-only.
- evaluate.test.ts locks that shape: "counts noOrigin for running briefs with zero forge refs and stays fail-open on the unscoped sweep (#4426)" expects code 0; "does not treat noOrigin as a non-zero unscoped verdict (#4426)" expects empty orphans and the all-clear line.
- packages/core/src/orphan-active/refs.ts collectGithubRefs matches only referenceTypeMatches(type, "github-issue") and "github-pr". Any other type, including x-xbrief/pull-request, contributes nothing.

Inventory: #3875 pr-closeout-attestable unwired and closing-reference triggered; #3791 sweep uses this evaluator; #3495 is the no-brief mirror. Do not recut collectGithubRefs as this finding. No implement and no ingest from this parent.

The recorded target does not survive as one default over both empty-ref briefs and dropped-ref briefs. The issue design can bind only if it partitions those classes and fail-closes the dropped-ref class. A new warn channel, a new no-origin marker, and a recut of collectGithubRefs are not this remedy.

## 1. Empty collect is two classes; #4426 already owns one of them — sharpens-framing

Evidence. Pin-read evaluate.ts at edf1d698aafcf956cff08ad3ad14ff608505861a: after collectGithubRefs, `if (issues.length === 0 && prs.length === 0) { noOrigin += 1; continue; }` never calls assessOrphanSignature. OrphanActiveBasis.noOrigin JSDoc says reporting only and does not change the two unknown policies. I re-ran evaluate.test.ts -t noOrigin: three tests passed. "counts noOrigin for running briefs with zero forge refs and stays fail-open on the unscoped sweep (#4426)" writes a running brief with only a title, expects code 0, scanned 2, noOrigin 1, and the Origins line. "does not treat noOrigin as a non-zero unscoped verdict (#4426)" writes two title-only running briefs, expects code 0, empty orphans, and the all-clear headline. content/docs/orphan-active-verdict-basis.md records noOrigin as #4426 reporting and forbids citing exit 0 with noOrigin > 0 as evidence those briefs are clean of shipped residue. CHANGELOG for #4426 is setup-created scopes: count unresolved origins, unscoped sweep stays fail-open, origin writes stay off the agent. I did not find a brief-level no-forge-origin marker. emit-hints none / umbrella / per-vBRIEF is an operator choice at emit time, not a field on the plan. assessOrphanSignature after the PR loop returns PASS when issueRefs.length === 0, so deleting the continue without a new branch still exits 0 for true originless.

Failure mode. Binding "an originless active/running brief should surface as its own finding kind" over the whole empty-collect set recuts #4426. Every running setup-created brief before issue:emit would become a finding. Check composition (Taskfile.yml check:framework-source and check:consumer) runs verify:orphan-active --changed-only; a fail-closed empty-ref class would redden those lanes for legitimate pre-emit work. Inventing the suggested marker is a new mechanism; empty references are already the #4426 signal.

Disposition. Bind only with a partition: empty collect with no github-shaped reference entries stays #4426 fail-open plus the Origins line. Empty collect that dropped reference entries is a different class (finding 2). Do not add a marker to make setup-created legal. Do not treat "cannot resolve" as one kind.

## 2. Warn already prints; P1 is the exit 0 skip of dropped refs — blocks-the-design

Evidence. The live reproduction in the issue body is the all-clear headline, Origins: 1 of 2, exit 0, while a running brief for already-merged work sat in active/. That is the Origins line working. packages/cli/src/verify-orphan-active.ts run() prints result.message and returns result.code. evaluate() returns code 1 only when orphans.length > 0; quiet success returns code 0 and an empty message. OrphanKind is only shipped | unresolved. Both fail closed. formatRefusal remediates shipped with scope:complete and unresolved with retry the GitHub lookup. I measured referenceTypeMatches("x-xbrief/pull-request", "github-pr") === false and the github-pr control true (tsx import of packages/types/src/reference.ts). collectGithubRefs only matches github-issue and github-pr. KNOWN_REFERENCE_TYPES has no pull-request spelling. The measured counterfactual (change only that type string, same gate fail-closes on linked PR merged) is dropped refs, not setup-created empty refs.

Failure mode. Deferring fail-closed versus warn leaves P1 in place. Warn is the current Origins line; agents and check consume exit code. Putting dropped refs into orphans[] is fail-closed in this evaluator. Reusing kind unresolved prints retry-the-lookup, which cannot recover a type collectGithubRefs ignored. Reusing kind shipped prints scope:complete, which is the wrong remedy when the origin string is sitting in the JSON unread. The existing prose forbid in verdict-basis.md is not a control: the measured miss printed Origins and still exited 0.

Disposition. The lean cannot bind while that verdict stays a later judgement. Bound remedy for this issue is a distinct finding class for dropped refs (unmatched reserved-namespace or unparseable github-shaped entries), exit 1, remediation to make the origin collectable (or companion #4698 at write time), not scope:complete and not retry. Empty-ref setup-created stays finding 1. Companion #4698 is inventory only; it does not close this skip.

Injection / swarm lens. The target changes gate authority over untrusted xBRIEF reference types. A reserved-namespace type string the matcher does not know currently fail-opens a gate composed into check:framework-source and check:consumer. That is the control to add, not a later reader of the Origins line.

## 3. Detection-was-ready is true only after collect returns the PR — sharpens-framing

Evidence. assessOrphanSignature unscoped: for each pr, skipGh continues, merged === true returns shipped. Then if issueRefs.length === 0 return PASS. A dropped PR never enters that loop. The "linked PR is merged" path is ready only when collectGithubRefs returned the PR. I did not recut collectGithubRefs as this finding; it is the producer of empty, not the continue/exit 0.

Failure mode. A bind that says "stop continuing and call assessOrphanSignature" still PASSes originless and still exits 0. A bind that only aliases pull-request still skip-continues every other unmatched type, a bad URI, and a missing defaultRepo.

Disposition. The skip site stays the continue/exit 0. The new class in finding 2 is a branch at that site, not a fall-through into assessOrphanSignature.

## 4. Neighboring gates and scoped scan — footnote

verify:pr-closeout-attestable is wired into pr:wait-mergeable wrappers.ts (evaluateCloseoutAttestable), not unwired. The issue's second half still holds: trigger is the PR closing reference; a dependency-upgrade PR with empty closingIssuesReferences is outside it. #3791 routes through this evaluator, so the skip follows the sweep. verify:completed-tracked also calls collectGithubRefs, so the same dropped type is missing there too. After #536, vbrief:validate D11 treats any ^x-xbrief/ type as an origin, so pull-request can satisfy D11 while this gate counts noOrigin. Scoped --issue N continues before scanned/noOrigin when briefReferencesIssue is false, so a malformed PR-only brief is invisible on the after-merge DONE gate, not even an Origins count. Quiet mode drops the Origins line on success; check does not pass --quiet.

## 5. Embedded instructions on the thread — footnote

Issue body "Do not silently continue" is the proposed shape, not a command to this critic. Comment 5715165110 is the companion pointer for #4698. Stop 1 process notes are already in the envelope. None were followed as instructions.

Road-not-taken. I considered aliasing x-xbrief/pull-request to github-pr inside collectGithubRefs (or teaching referenceTypeMatches a synonym). Strongest case: the measured counterfactual was one type string; the alias would have reached the existing merged-PR shipped path without recutting #4426 fail-open. Rejected because the next unknown reserved-namespace spelling, an unparseable URI, and a missing defaultRepo still hit the same continue/exit 0, and the write-side close of the reserved namespace is companion #4698. What would flip: a measured miss that is only that one spelling, with evidence no other dropped-ref shape occurs.

Steelman of the target. Counting noOrigin and exiting 0 is the correct default for setup-created and other never-origin-keyed running briefs: the unscoped sweep must not make offline or pre-emit work network-authorized (#3767 / #4426), and those briefs are not orphans under the shipped signature. The Origins line plus the verdict-basis forbid already tell a careful reader the pass is not evidence. Flip: the measured consumer miss is dropped refs, not setup-created; the all-clear headline and exit 0 are the consumed verdict; the forbid is documentation; check still composes this evaluator.
